title: Streamlining Virtual Machine Storage Lifecycle
business: Enterprises running high-availability Linux virtual machines for internal applications.
problem: Manual management of storage accounts and underlying VHD files leads to operational overhead and potential data consistency issues during scaling operations.
solution: Azure Managed Disks abstract the storage account management layer, providing block-level storage volumes that are automatically handled by the Azure platform, simplifying attachment and snapshotting processes.
steps: Provision a new Linux virtual machine specifying the managed disk option.
Define the disk size and performance tier requirements within the VM configuration.
Attach additional data disks to the virtual machine via the Azure portal or CLI.
Utilize platform-managed snapshots to create point-in-time backups of the disks.
outcome: Reduced administrative burden and improved reliability for disk lifecycle management without manual storage account orchestration.
limitation: Managed disks are tied to the lifecycle of the virtual machine; deleting the VM may result in the deletion of attached managed disks unless explicitly configured otherwise. Check the 'Delete option' setting in the VM resource properties.

questions.question: In Streamlining Virtual Machine Storage Lifecycle, what is the primary benefit of using Azure Managed Disks?
options: Automatic handling of storage account management
Unlimited storage capacity per virtual machine
Elimination of the need for virtual machine backups
Lowering the cost of compute resources
questions.explanation: The solution explicitly states that Managed Disks abstract the storage account management layer, which is the primary operational benefit.
questions.evidence: Azure Managed Disks abstract the storage account management layer, providing block-level storage volumes that are automatically handled by the Azure platform

questions.question: In Streamlining Virtual Machine Storage Lifecycle, what is a key limitation regarding disk persistence?
options: Managed disks cannot be resized after creation
Managed disks are tied to the lifecycle of the virtual machine
Managed disks require manual storage account configuration
Managed disks only support Windows operating systems
questions.explanation: The limitation section notes that managed disks are tied to the VM lifecycle, meaning deletion of the VM can impact the disk.
questions.evidence: Managed disks are tied to the lifecycle of the virtual machine; deleting the VM may result in the deletion of attached managed disks unless explicitly configured otherwise.
